Why it exists

Most of us now live somewhere our grandparents did not. Bluxe Century began by writing for the African diaspora, and found a story that belongs to anyone who has made a life across borders.

The foundation is African: Dame-Dame, the Adinkra symbol of intelligence, ingenuity and strategy. The conversation is international: property, people, technology, travel, lifestyle and culture, told for readers of every background who value thought, character, creativity and progress.

The idea and heritage

Intelligence. Ingenuity. Strategy.

Three principles carried by one symbol, and the reason a magazine founded in London speaks to readers everywhere.

The symbol

Dame-Dame

Adinkra is a visual language of the Akan peoples of present-day Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Its symbols are printed on cloth, carved and cast, and each one carries a proverb or a principle.

Dame-Dame takes its name and form from a board game of the draughts family. A game won by reading the board, anticipating the other side and choosing the right move. Its meaning follows: intelligence, ingenuity and strategy.

Inside Bluxe, this inheritance has a name of its own: the wisdom of Akibuland, the ancient African source the brand draws on. Dame-Dame is its central mark. We reproduce it exactly as drawn, in black or white, and never redraw it.

From principle to page

What the three words do.

Intelligence

Read the board

We report the forces behind wealth, culture and movement, and say why they matter. Sources sit beside the numbers.

Ingenuity

Find the new move

New formats when the old ones stop working: territory supplements, the MagCast, The Grapevine briefing.

Strategy

Play for the long game

Stories that lead somewhere: an introduction, a partnership, an event, a decision made with better information.

African in origin

Universal in use.

Draughts is played on the same board in Accra, Lisbon, Lagos and Kuala Lumpur. The rules do not ask where you are from.

Bluxe Century celebrates its African origin openly and writes for anyone who values thought, character, creativity and progress. Readers do not need to belong to a particular place, background or income bracket to use the ideas. They need curiosity.

History

From The Estate to Bluxe Century.

The platform began as a property guide for the diaspora and grew, edition by edition, into an international media platform. The identity changed with it.

  1. The beginning

    The Estate Property Guide

    Founded to connect members of the diaspora worldwide and to challenge negative imagery of African people. Early issues featured Cape Verde, Kensington and investing in Africa, then Morocco’s Atlas Mountains and Deborah Meaden.

  2. A wider remit

    The Estate

    The third edition dropped the former title. Lifestyle interviews joined property, including a CBRE guide to buying in London.

  3. 2018

    Nelson Mandela centenary edition

    A special edition with contributions from Graça Machel, Lonnie Bunch III, Freddie Achom and Ray Stowers.

  4. Events and community

    From page to room

    African art at the US Embassy, Savile Row gatherings, a Soneva Fushi conversation on sustainable luxury, early crypto at Gieves & Hawkes, and the launch of Bluxe membership.

  5. 2022

    Bluxe Century

    The Estate became Bluxe Century: an annual publication under the Dame-Dame mark, with a view across Africa, Asia, the Gulf and Europe.

  6. 2023 – 2024

    Annuals and supplements

    The 2023 Annual, the Mauritius supplement and the 2024 Annual, The Year of Adventure.

  7. 2026

    Vol. 07 and the MagCast

    A digital Annual of seventeen stories, The Grapevine briefing and the MagCast, a format for serious ideas in audio, text and image.

The media platform

Connected parts of one point of view.

A magazine, territory supplements, digital editorial and film, and a network that meets in person. Here is what each one offers readers, and what it offers the partners it suits.

01 · The Annual

Bluxe Century magazine

The main annual publication. Property, people, technology, travel, lifestyle and culture, read through a Bluxe lens.

For readers

Long-form stories with room to explain a market, a place or a person, published as a digital edition you can read on any screen.

For partners

Space for substantial storytelling: covers, editorial features, branded content and advertising within the subjects your audience already reads.

Open the reading room

02 · Regional supplements

One territory at a time.

Each supplement focuses on a single territory: its people, businesses, experiences and the reasons to pay attention.

For readers

A considered introduction to a country, written for people deciding whether to visit, invest or build there.

For partners

Market entry, destination promotion and locally relevant campaigns, built around a specific brief with a tourism body, investor or brand.

The Mauritius supplement is published. Portugal, Japan, Malaysia, Rwanda, Bahrain and Hong Kong are designed and in development; each is open to a partnership conversation.

04 · Network and experiences

Where readers meet.

Bluxe Century sits within the wider Bluxe world: a curated membership network and gatherings that bring readers, founders and brands into the same room.

For readers

Invitations, introductions and access through Bluxe membership, which is separate from reading the magazine and is by application.

For partners

Hosted conversations, launches and VIP experiences, where appropriate, with the people a story was written for.

How membership works

Beyond placement

Repackaging for relevance.

Some brands need more than an advert. Bluxe Century can interpret a brand for an audience: understand what a partner offers, then express it in a language and setting its readers recognise.

That is the phrase the 2024 media pack uses. In practice it draws on brand strategy experience: audience, positioning and presentation, applied to a wider brief than media space alone. The Africa Fashion Week London repositioning is the clearest documented example.

      Track record

      What Bluxe has built.

      Documented work from the platform’s history. These are past results, reported by Bluxe, and they are not a forecast of current platform performance.

      Case study

      Africa Fashion Week London.

      Historical client result

      The challenge

      A new buyer audience

      Founded in 2011, AFWL had built a following as a platform for African fashion. The next step was commercial: reach buyers with spending power, and make the event pay for its ambition.

      The approach

      Reposition, then rebuild the offer

      Bluxe repositioned the event for a new demographic and developed new revenue streams. The 2019 materials also document institutional participation in the wider event.

      The formats

      Reasons to attend and to pay

      Corporate hospitality and a VIP area, a luxury and premium boutique area, a business consumer forum, a charity celebrity fashion show, an African food village and souk, and live music.

      Reported outcomes

      78%

      Increase in sponsorship and advertising revenue

      127%

      Increase in exhibitor sales

      205%

      Increase in event profit

      Figures as reported in the Bluxe Africa Fashion Week London case study. Historical results for one client; they show Bluxe’s approach to positioning, audience development and commercial execution, and are not a forecast for advertisers.

      Relevance, with context.

      Bluxe Century introduces a brand through a story, a territory, a film or a room of the right people. The value is relevance, trust and attention that lasts longer than a scroll.

      Request a proposalDownload the packs

      Ways to work together

      Three kinds of partner.

      Advertiser

      Be seen in the right company

      Place a product or service in a publication whose subjects and readers are relevant to it.

      • Cover and inside-cover positions
      • Single pages and double-page spreads
      • Placement in a regional supplement
      • Digital placement and newsletter inclusion

      Brand

      Have your story told well

      For brands whose quality needs explanation: property, hospitality, travel, design, technology, wealth services and considered lifestyle products.

      • Editorial features, 4 to 8 page equivalent
      • Branded content and visual presentation
      • Film and an optional MagCast feature
      • Social amplification

      Strategic partner

      Build something together

      A broader relationship developed around a specific brief, rather than a fixed package.

      • A regional supplement or destination narrative
      • An editorial series
      • An event or VIP experience
      • Distribution or a joint initiative

      Formats are developed around each brief. Availability, scale and rates are confirmed in a current proposal.
